item.text: The seed has 158 lines. I’m preserving its main boundaries and flows while expanding retry behavior, live selection, and context handling in peripheral trees. The source also clarifies two details: an exec result is evicted from the request cache only when it has a version and no transaction, and context readiness depends on fingerprints rather than successful materialization.

item.text: The central tree is now 108 lines and 7,072 characters: 32% fewer lines and 34% fewer characters. Six peripheral trees add source-backed details, including copy capability checks, selection limits, reply failures, jump validation, and single-diagram saves. I’m checking their spacing and edge anchors now.

{
  "explanation": "The central tree retains the shared boundary, routing, ownership and data dependencies while shrinking from 158 to 108 lines (31.6%) and from 10,646 to 7,072 characters (33.6%). Six peripherals expand meaningful concept lines. M = modular structure, C = calls, O = ownership, D = data dependency. These are complementary views; D records computational prerequisites. Cross-diagram edges indicate expansion, not necessarily runtime calls. Positions use measured text dimensions with at least 14 columns between diagram columns and eight rows between stacked peripherals.

Two seed claims are narrowed by the implementation. First, sessionService.ts:186-189 evicts resolved exec requests only when the result contains version and lacks transaction; unbound reads without version do not qualify.
